name: Diablo
description: Diablo is a high-action Five Card Draw poker variant characterized by three primary mechanics: Deuces are wild, players are restricted to drawing a maximum of two cards, and most importantly, if the player who opens the betting fails to win the pot, they must 'match the pot' to create a new one for the next deal.

overview.description: Diablo is a high-action Five Card Draw poker variant characterized by three primary mechanics: Deuces are wild, players are restricted to drawing a maximum of two cards, and most importantly, if the player who opens the betting fails to win the pot, they must 'match the pot' to create a new one for the next deal.

history.origins: A staple of 'Dealer's Choice' home games in the United States. Its exact origin is undocumented, but it belongs to the mid-20th century tradition of 'action-inducing' poker variants.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Diablo emerges in social poker circles.
2010: First documented in English-language card-game references as a Draw Poker variant.
history.cultural: Known as a 'pot-builder' or 'destroyer of bankrolls' in casual settings.
history.evolution: Derived from Standard Five Card Draw, the 'Diablo' element was added to ensure pots grow exponentially and to penalize marginal openers.

setup.players: 2-6 players (Best with 5-6 to ensure enough competition for the opener).
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. All four 2s are wild.
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 5 cards face down. In some variants, the first replacement card drawn later is dealt face up, though standard Diablo keeps all cards face down (verify with house rules).

rules.objective: Make the best five-card poker hand using Deuces as wild cards. In Diablo mode, the opener must win the pot or match it to fund the next hand.
rules.gameplay:
1. Ante: Standard ante from all players.
2. Deal: 5 cards to each player.
3. First Betting Round: Standard poker betting begun by player to dealer's left.
4. The Draw: Active players may discard and draw a MAXIMUM of two cards.
5. Second Betting Round: Standard betting begun by the player who opened the first round.
6. Showdown: Best hand wins the pot.
7. Diablo rule: If the opener does not win, the opener contributes an amount equal to the just-won pot to seed the next hand. Deal passes left and the next hand is played with no new antes. The cycle continues until a hand in which the opener wins.
keyRules: Openers must win or match the pot.
Standard poker hand rankings with Five of a Kind as highest hand.

strategy.basic: Be extremely cautious about opening the pot. If your hand is marginal, checking is safer to avoid the 'Match the Pot' penalty.
strategy.intermediate: Since everyone knows Deuces are wild, 'Trips' are the new 'Pair.' Don't bother staying in the hand without at least a natural pair or a wild card.
strategy.advanced: Positional opening: If you are the dealer and it's checked to you, opening is less risky because you have seen everyone else's lack of interest. However, if you open and lose, you pay. Use the threat of the 'Match' to force folds if you have a strong hand.
tips: Don't open on a bluff unless you have the chips to cover a pot-match.
If you hold two deuces, you have a powerhouse - opening is usually correct.
Track the 'Diablo' pot size; it can grow very fast.

variations.name: Capped Diablo
variations.description: To prevent bankrupting players, the amount the opener must match is capped at a fixed limit (e.g., 20 big blinds).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Override would set a cap constant; not yet mapped in engine.constants.

variations.name: Exposed Diablo
variations.description: The first card drawn by each player is dealt face up, providing more information to the table.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Override would change card visibility in draw phase; not yet mapped.

scoring.description: Pot-based cash game. Winner of each hand takes the pot. Diablo mechanism creates escalating pots.
scoring.winCondition: Player with highest 5-card poker hand at showdown wins the current pot. If the opener loses, the opener matches the just-won pot to create the next hand's carryover pot.

synthesis.shortDescription: A volatile Five Card Draw variant where wild deuces, restricted draws, and the Diablo penalty (openers must match the pot if they lose) create exponentially growing pots and high-action betting.

hero.title: DIABLO
hero.subtitle: The Pot-Escalating Draw Poker
hero.tagline: Deuces wild. Maximum 2-card draw. Openers must win or match the pot.
